run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-16T18:09:13Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for fraud-detection is explained by error-status spans the service emits on its gRPC streaming client to flagd. In the last observable data (span metrics up to 17:37-17:39Z, traces to about 17:29-17:30Z) every ERROR span attributed to service_name=fraud-detection is a flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream client span, plus a few flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt ones: error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, duration about 600 s, with the flagd-side child span either OK or reporting the exact text 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'. At 17:39:00Z fraud-detection summed 5 ERROR against 25 UNSET spans (ratio 0.1667), the highest error ratio of the nine services returning data. The same EventStream error pattern exists for ad (8) and recommendation (7), so it is a flagd-client-wide stream behaviour, not unique to fraud-detection. Nothing points to a pod-level failure: 10/10 fraud-detection pods and the flagd pod are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, no OOMKilled/Evicted/Unhealthy event was returned for them, nodes show no pressure, and the Kafka consumer spans carry no error status. Important limits: span-metric samples stop at about 17:37-17:39Z and traces at about 17:30Z, i.e. before the 18:09:13Z alert, and the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, so neither the reported 0.0222 value nor the continuation of the error stream at alert time could be re-verified; attribution between a flagd-side stream timeout and a client-side 600 s deadline remains partially unresolved.

claims.text: At the last available evaluation (2026-11-16T17:39:00Z) the span counters for service_name=fraud-detection sum to 5 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 25 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans; the only ERROR series for this service are span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt (the other span names present are orders process, orders receive and resolve, all UNSET).

At 2026-11-16T17:39:00Z the ERROR/total span ratio of fraud-detection is 0.1667, higher than every other service returning data: payment 0.0589, frontend-proxy 0.0585, ad 0.0369, frontend 0.0317, shipping 0.0179, checkout 0.00516, accounting 0.00505, recommendation 0.00330.

Every error trace returned for fraud-detection in the 24 h search (10 traces, 19 spans) is a flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream call: the fraud-detection client spans carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 with durations 594,101,234-601,796,702 µs and no parent reference, while the child spans of service flagd (version v0.12.8) carry 7 with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and 2 with error=true and otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout'.

Trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 contains exactly two spans: the fraud-detection EventStream client span (duration 599,999,905 µs, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, ERROR) and its visible child span in service flagd (duration 553,397,947 µs, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, otel.status_description 'stream closed due to server-side timeout').

The fraud-detection ERROR counters reached the value 1 on each of 12 distinct series between 17:26Z and 17:39Z (10 flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream series, each with its own exported_instance value, plus flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt on 2 exported_instance values) and then stayed constant in the observed data.
The flagd EventStream error pattern is not exclusive to fraud-detection: at 2026-11-16T17:39:00Z the EventStream ERROR counter sums were ad 8, recommendation 7 and fraud-detection 4.

Kubernetes state: the fraud-detection Deployment is 10/10 available/ready with all 10 pods on ReplicaSet fraud-detection-9fb7d885b (created 17:13:14Z), Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 17:13:15-17:16:18Z; the flagd Deployment is 1/1 ready with pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx Running/Ready, restartCount 0, started 17:15:07Z.

flagd revision 2 (ReplicaSet flagd-58db7486bd, created 17:15:07Z) replaced revision 1 (flagd-c47676d99, created 17:13:14Z, now 0 replicas); both pod templates are identical - image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8, command /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json, same env and same config-rw/config-ro volumes - so no flagd configuration difference is visible between the two revisions.

The Kubernetes events returned for the window (28 items, timestamped 17:28:32-17:31:36Z) contain no event whose involved object is a flagd or fraud-detection pod, ReplicaSet or Deployment; they are HorizontalPodAutoscaler FailedGetResourceMetric / FailedComputeMetricsReplicas warnings for kafka, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart plus recommendation scale-down and Killing events.

Observable telemetry stops before the alert instant: the span-metric points used here end at 17:37:21Z-17:39:00Z (last returned sample times) and the Jaeger results report data_as_of about 17:29:36Z-17:30:26Z, while the alert is dated 2026-11-16T18:09:13Z, so no sample exists at the alert time.

Pod-level fault is not supported as the cause: every fraud-detection container and both flagd containers report ready=true with restartCount 0, no event returned by the events query concerns a fraud-detection or flagd object (no OOMKilled, Evicted or Unhealthy), and all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

No error signal was observed on fraud-detection's Kafka consumption path or in its own request handling: the only span names for the service in Jaeger are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (client), orders receive and orders process (consumer), and the order trace examined has no status tags and no error detail.

The hypothesis that the alert is produced by a fraud-detection crash loop, OOM kill or eviction is rejected: restartCount is 0 on all 10 fraud-detection containers and on both flagd containers, no eviction/OOM/Unhealthy event was returned for them, and all pods are Running and Ready.

The alert is driven by these flagd EventStream client spans: each stream lives about 600 s and then ends in gRPC status 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), which the spanmetrics connector counts as STATUS_CODE_ERROR for service_name=fraud-detection; together with a small number of flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt errors this is the only error population the service produces, and because its other spans are Kafka consumer spans it is a large share of the service's span total (0.1667 in the last cumulative sample), consistent with a ratio alert of the order of the reported 0.0222.

The deepest trigger the evidence shows is flagd closing the gRPC EventStream: the flagd-side span of the same stream records rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and the exact diagnostic text 'stream closed due to server-side timeout', and the identical EventStream error pattern is present for other flagd clients (ad 8, recommendation 7 error counters at 17:39), i.e. the stream teardown originates on the flagd server side rather than in fraud-detection's business logic.

An alternative explanation that remains open is a client-side deadline mismatch in the flagd client used by fraud-detection: the client span lasts 599,999,905 µs against a flagd-side span of 553,397,947 µs, and in 7 of the 9 sampled client/server pairs the flagd span ended with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 while the client still reported DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, so part of the ERROR status may come from the client's about 600 s stream deadline rather than from a flagd failure.

gaps: No telemetry exists at or after the alert start 2026-11-16T18:09:13Z: span-metric samples stop at about 17:37-17:39Z and Jaeger results at about 17:29-17:30Z, so the reported current value 0.0222 and whether the EventStream error stream continued to 18:09 cannot be verified.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and an empty rule set), so the exact expression, evaluation window and threshold that produced 0.0222 are unknown.

Application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data with 0 lines for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l and for flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx, so the client-side reconnect behaviour and flagd's stream-timeout configuration are unverified (flagd runs with no explicit stream-timeout flag visible in its command line).

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_container_info, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_pod_owner) returned no data in this Prometheus and get_prometheus_target listed no active scrape targets (status no_data), so scrape health at incident time and image-digest change history could not be checked through metrics.

The change_history integration is not available, so a change-based explanation (for example a flagd or fraud-detection configuration change) could not be tested; only the API snapshot shows an identical flagd pod template across revisions 1 and 2.
Whether this flagd EventStream timeout behaviour predates the current pods (created 17:13-17:16Z) is unknown: no earlier baseline exists in the available telemetry.
The ResolveInt ERROR counter (value 1 on two series) has no corresponding span visible in the returned error traces, so its exact cause is not established.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition (expression, window, threshold) to confirm it computes a span error ratio and to see whether long-lived stream spans are intentionally counted.

Review flagd server-side stream/keepalive timeout settings and the flagd Go client stream-deadline handling in fraud-detection 2.1.3, and consider aligning the client deadline with the server's stream lifetime or excluding the EventStream span from error-rate accounting.
Collect fresh logs from a live fraud-detection pod and the flagd pod (empty in this run) to confirm why the stream is closed after about 550-600 s and whether the client reconnects cleanly.
Re-evaluate the fraud-detection error ratio after 18:22Z once new samples are scraped, to confirm the alert value and whether the pattern persists.
